mainTopic: Taking goods on approval (borrower or paid watchman), vows about 'ערלים' and 'מולים', and the greatness of מילה
overview: The גמרא settles a contradiction: our משנה is about an average sale, while שמואל is about an in-demand sale, where the buyer gains. A ברייתא supports שמואל. A man who takes utensils on approval to send to his father-in-law pays for an accident on the way there, like a borrower, but is exempt on the way back, like a paid watchman. רב נחמן made a middleman pay for an accident on the way back. When רבא challenges him, he answers that a middleman's return trip still counts as the trip out, since he would sell the item even at his own door. A new משנה rules that in a vow, 'ערלים' means non-Jews and 'מולים' means Jews, whatever their physical state, and proves this from פסוקים. The משנה then lists many praises of מילה, each opening with 'גדולה מילה'. In the גמרא, a ברייתא says משה's merits did not protect him when he was lax about מילה. רבי insists משה was not lax but was caught in a real bind. The גמרא then asks why משה was punished, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Average sale versus in-demand sale
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles the contradiction between the משנה and שמואל by saying they deal with two different kinds of sales.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is talking about an ordinary sale. שמואל is talking about a sale of goods that are in high demand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a contradiction by saying the משנה and שמואל are talking about two different kinds of sales.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In an ordinary sale at the fixed price, neither buyer nor seller gains more, so the person who made the נדר must adjust the price to avoid giving benefit. With in-demand goods, the buyer is the one who gains, so שמואל can treat a buyer who takes the item to inspect it like a borrower. Once each source is placed in its own kind of sale, the two no longer clash.

keyTerms.meaning: A sale, or merchandise being sold
Average, middle quality; neither hard to sell nor in demand
Sharp, keen; goods in high demand that sell quickly

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is rejecting the משנה or rejecting שמואל. Both rules stay true. Each one applies to a different kind of sale.

phrases.english: Our משנה is dealing with an average sale,
phrases.notes: An average sale means goods that are neither hard to sell nor in special demand.

phrases.english: and שמואל's case is dealing with a keen, in-demand sale.
phrases.notes: In a sale like this, the buyer is the one who mainly gains.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction between the משנה and שמואל that was raised just before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source refers to a different type of sale.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed both sources describe the same kind of sale, so they seemed to disagree about who benefits.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about an average sale, where neither side gains more. שמואל is about an in-demand sale, where the buyer gains.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports שמואל: taking goods on approval
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a man who takes utensils from a merchant to send to his father-in-law must pay if they are lost by accident on the way there.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports שמואל. A man took utensils from a merchant to send to his father-in-law. He told the merchant: if they accept them, I will pay you full price, and if not, I will pay you for the benefit I got from them. If the utensils were destroyed by accident on the way there, he must pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up שמואל: someone who takes goods to try them out is liable, even for an accident, while he is getting use out of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally only a שואל (borrower) has to pay for an אונס (an accident he could not prevent). On the way to his father-in-law, the man is using the utensils for his own benefit, to honor his father-in-law. So he is treated like a borrower, which is exactly what שמואל said.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא teaches in line with his view
A small benefit worth something; here, the goodwill he gained by showing the gift
They were destroyed by אונס, an accident beyond his control

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule the rest of the section turns on: on the way there you are like a borrower, and on the way back you are not.

phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא in accordance with שמואל:
One who takes utensils from a merchant
to send them to his father-in-law's house,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר לוֹ: אִם מְקַבְּלִין אוֹתָן מִמֶּנִּי —
phrases.english: and says to him: If they accept them from me,
I will give you their price,
and if not, I will give you
according to the benefit that I got from them.
phrases.notes: He means paying something for the honor he got from showing his father-in-law the gift.

phrases.english: If they were destroyed by accident on the way there, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that שמואל's rule is in place, the גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports it.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view that someone who takes goods on approval, while benefiting from them, is like a borrower and must pay even for an accident.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about utensils sent to the father-in-law: an accident on the way there makes him liable.

steps.title: On the way back he is only a paid watchman
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: if the utensils are destroyed by accident on the return trip, he is exempt, because now he is only like a שומר שכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the accident happened on the way back, he does not have to pay, because he is like a paid watchman.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its ruling: once the father-in-law turns down the gift, the man is no longer benefiting, so an accident on the way back does not make him pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His status changes in the middle of the case. Going there, he benefits, so he is like a שואל. Coming back, he no longer benefits, so he is only like a שומר שכר, and a paid watchman does not pay for an אונס.

keyTerms.meaning: A paid watchman (שומר שכר), who does not pay for accidents

steps.whatToRemember: Going there, he is like a borrower and pays even for an accident. Coming back, he is like a paid watchman and is exempt from paying for an accident.

phrases.english: If it happened on the return trip, he is exempt,
because he is like a paid watchman.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּחֲזָרָה פָּטוּר מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא כְּנוֹשֵׂא שָׂכָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the second half of the same ברייתא. It sets the return trip against the trip there.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An accident on the return trip is exempt, because the would-be buyer is then only like a שומר שכר.

steps.title: The middleman's case: רב נחמן makes him pay
steps.stepSummary: A middleman took a donkey to sell and could not sell it. On his way back, an accident happened to the donkey, and רב נחמן ruled that he must pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain middleman took a donkey to sell, but it did not sell. While he was returning it, an accident happened to the donkey, and רב נחמן obligated him to pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case that seems to go against the ברייתא. It is setting up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The accident happened on the return trip, just like the second half of the ברייתא. Even so, רב נחמן made the middleman pay. This sets up an obvious tension with the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: A middleman or broker who sells goods for others

phrases.english: There was a certain middleman
who took a donkey to sell
and it was not sold.
While he was returning, an accident happened to the donkey,
and רב נחמן obligated him to pay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a practical ruling that looks like it goes against the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן ruled that a middleman must pay for an accident that happened while he was returning goods he could not sell.

steps.title: רבא challenges רב נחמן from the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects: the ברייתא says an accident on the return trip is exempt, so why did רב נחמן make the middleman pay?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא raised an objection to רב נחמן: we learned that an accident on the way there makes him liable, but on the way back he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן's ruling by quoting the ברייתא. רב נחמן answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The middleman's accident happened on the way back, which the ברייתא clearly exempts. So רב נחמן's ruling looks like it goes directly against an earlier source. The גמרא now needs to explain how the two fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him from an earlier source

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not quoting a new source. He is quoting the same ברייתא from steps 2 and 3, using its ruling about the return trip.

phrases.english: רבא raised an objection to רב נחמן:
If an accident happened on the way there, he is liable;
if it happened on the return trip, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's ruling in step 4, using the ברייתא from steps 2 and 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that the middleman must pay for an accident on the return trip.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says that on the return trip the person is only like a paid watchman and does not pay for accidents. The middleman's case also happened on the return trip, so he should be exempt.

steps.title: A middleman's trip home still counts as the trip out
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers רבא: for a middleman, the return trip is treated like the trip out, because he would still sell the item if he found a buyer, even at his own door.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: when a middleman comes back, that is still part of the going out. After all, if he found someone to buy the donkey, even at the door of his own house, wouldn't he sell it to him?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא's challenge from Step 5. He explains why the ברייתא's rule about the return trip does not apply to a middleman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the son-in-law's purpose ends once the gift is refused, so on the way back he is only guarding the utensils. A middleman is different: his job is selling, and he keeps trying to sell all the way home. So he is still using the donkey for his own business, and he stays fully responsible even on the way back.

keyTerms.meaning: A middleman or broker who takes goods to sell for the owner
The trip out, going toward the goal

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's exemption on the way back only applies when the purpose of the trip is truly over. A סַפְסִירָא's purpose, selling, is never over until he gets home, so he still pays for an accident on the way back.

phrases.english: He said to him: the return trip of a middleman
is the trip out.
For if he would find someone to sell it to,
phrases.notes: "He" is the middleman, and "it" is the donkey from רב נחמן's case in Step 4.

phrases.english: even at the door of his house,
would he not sell it to him?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲזָרָה דְסַפְסִירָא הוֹלָכָה הִיא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: the middleman's purpose continues on the way home, while the son-in-law's purpose has ended
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every return trip is like the ברייתא, where the person is only a שומר שכר and is exempt from accidents
steps.terutzMaskana: A סַפְסִירָא's return is still part of his selling trip, so he stays fully liable

steps.title: A vow against benefiting from 'the uncircumcised' or 'the circumcised'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules: a vow against benefiting from ערלים forbids non-Jews and permits Jews. A vow against benefiting from מולים forbids Jews and permits non-Jews, whether or not they are actually circumcised.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says, 'Benefit from the uncircumcised is קונם for me,' he may benefit from uncircumcised Jews, but he may not benefit from circumcised non-Jews. If he says, 'Benefit from the circumcised is קונם for me,' he may not benefit from uncircumcised Jews, but he may benefit from circumcised non-Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules on two vows where the words 'ערלים' and 'מולים' are judged by how people normally use them, not by the physical facts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Jew who is not circumcised (for example, because of a medical danger) is still counted among the 'מולים', because the word means the Jewish people. A non-Jew who is circumcised is still counted among the 'ערלים', because the word means the nations. The next step gives the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: A substitute word for קרבן, used to make a vow that forbids something
The uncircumcised; here, the non-Jewish nations
The circumcised; here, the Jewish people
The nations of the world, meaning non-Jews

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the vow by the physical facts. 'ערלים' means non-Jews and 'מולים' means Jews, so an uncircumcised Jew still counts as 'מול'.

phrases.english: MISHNA: 'Benefit from the uncircumcised is konam for me':
he is permitted with uncircumcised Jews,
and forbidden with circumcised people of the nations of the world.
'That I benefit from the circumcised':
phrases.notes: The word 'קונם' carries over from the first case, so he's making the same kind of vow.

phrases.english: he is forbidden with uncircumcised Jews,
and permitted with circumcised people of the nations of the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new subject
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a vow, 'ערלים' means non-Jews and 'מולים' means Jews, no matter what their actual physical state is

steps.title: Proof from פסוקים that 'ערלה' is a name for the nations
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains its ruling: the word ערלה is used only as a name for the nations. It proves this from three פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'uncircumcised' is used only as a name for the nations of the world. As it says: 'For all the nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel are uncircumcised in the heart.' It also says: 'And this uncircumcised Philistine shall be.' And it says: 'Lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה backs up its ruling by showing how the תנ״ך uses the word 'ערל'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first פסוק, the nations are called 'ערלים' without any qualification, while Israel is only 'ערלי לב', uncircumcised of the heart. The other two פסוקים use 'ערל' as a plain description of the פלשתים. So 'ערל' works as a name for non-Jews, and the vow follows that meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: Foreskin; here, the state of being uncircumcised as a label
Uncircumcised of the heart, meaning spiritually closed

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין הָעׇרְלָה קְרוּיָה אֶלָּא לְשֵׁם אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם,
phrases.english: For 'uncircumcised' is used only as a name for the nations of the world,
as it is said: 'For all the nations are uncircumcised,'
phrases.notes: ירמיהו ט:כה

phrases.english: 'and all the house of Israel are uncircumcised in the heart.'
And it says: 'And this uncircumcised Philistine shall be.'
phrases.notes: שמואל א יז:לו

phrases.english: And it says: 'Lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice,'
phrases.notes: שמואל ב א:כ

phrases.english: 'lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph.'

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאֵין הָעׇרְלָה קְרוּיָה אֶלָּא לְשֵׁם אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason and the proof for the ruling in Step 7
steps.raayaObject: That in a vow, 'ערלים' means non-Jews and not physically uncircumcised Jews
steps.raayaSupportSource: ירמיהו ט:כה; שמואל א יז:לו; שמואל ב א:כ

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: the ערלה is disgusting
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says the ערלה is repulsive, since the wicked are shamed by it, as the פסוק calls the nations 'ערלים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: The foreskin is repulsive, because the wicked were shamed through it, as it says: 'For all the nations are uncircumcised.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a statement praising מילה by showing how disgraceful the ערלה is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses the same פסוק from Step 8, but for a new purpose. There it proved how the word is used. Here it shows that being called 'ערל' is a mark of shame on the wicked, so the ערלה itself is something disgusting.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:
The foreskin is repulsive,
since the wicked were disgraced through it,
as it is said: 'For all the nations are uncircumcised.'
phrases.notes: This is the same פסוק from ירמיהו that the משנה quoted just before.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמֵר: מְאוּסָה הִיא הָעׇרְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reuses the פסוק from Step 8 to show that the ערלה is a disgrace
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ערלה is repulsive, because the wicked are disgraced by being called 'ערלים'

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: מילה is great
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל says מילה is great, because thirteen covenants were made over it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: Circumcision is great, for thirteen covenants were made over it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second praise of מילה, this time from רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה praised מילה by showing the shame of its opposite. רבי ישמעאל praises מילה directly, by its many covenants. This opens a series of 'גדולה מילה' statements.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says:
Great is circumcision,
for thirteen covenants were made over it.
phrases.notes: This points to the word 'ברית', which shows up thirteen times in the מילה section of בראשית יז.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second praise of מילה, which goes along with Step 9
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מילה is great, because thirteen covenants were made over it

steps.title: רבי יוסי: circumcision overrides שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says מילה is great because it pushes aside the strict laws of שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: Circumcision is great, because it overrides the strict שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The list of praises for מילה continues. רבי יוסי gives his reason: a ברית on the eighth day is done even on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שבת is very severe, and cutting is normally forbidden on it. If the eighth day falls on שבת, the ברית still happens. That shows how important מילה is.

keyTerms.meaning: Great is circumcision. This is the opening phrase repeated by each תנא in this list

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: Great is circumcision,
for it overrides the strict Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another תנא's reason to the משנה's list of praises for מילה, after רבי ישמעאל's in Step 10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מילה is great because it overrides the severe laws of שבת.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן קרחה: משה was punished right away for delaying it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן קרחה says מילה is great because משה was not given even one full hour of delay when he put off his son's מילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן קרחה says: Circumcision is great, because משה הצדיק was not given even a full hour's delay over it.
steps.whatsHappening: Another תנא praises מילה. He points out that even a great צדיק like משה was punished right away for delaying it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'לא נתלה לו מלא שעה' mean משה's punishment was not held off for even a full hour. Even a צדיק as great as משה was punished at once. That shows how seriously the Torah treats putting off a ברית.

keyTerms.meaning: Was held off or postponed (here: the punishment)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha says:
Great is circumcision,
for Moses the righteous was not given a delay
phrases.notes: This refers to the story in שמות 4:24–26, when משה was in danger for not doing his son's ברית.

phrases.english: over it, even for a full hour.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה אוֹמֵר: גְּדוֹלָה מִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another reason added to the same list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מילה is great because even משה was punished at once for delaying it.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה: circumcision overrides the laws of leprous marks
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה says מילה is great because it pushes aside the laws of נגעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה says: Circumcision is great, because it overrides the laws of leprous marks.
steps.whatsHappening: Another תנא praises מילה. He says it even pushes aside the laws of נגעים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is normally forbidden to cut off a נגע. If a נגע is on the ערלה, the ברית is still done, even though that cuts the נגע away. So מילה wins out over that prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: Marks of צרעת (often translated 'leprosy') that have special Torah laws

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya says: Great is circumcision,
for it overrides the laws of leprous marks.
phrases.notes: He means that if a נגע is on the ערלה, you still do the ברית, even though cutting a נגע is normally forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Like רבי יוסי in Step 11, he shows that מילה overrides another law, this time נגעים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מילה is great because it overrides the prohibition of cutting off a נגע.

steps.title: רבי: אברהם was not called complete until he was circumcised
steps.stepSummary: רבי says that even with all of אברהם's מצוות, he was not called 'complete' until he had his מילה, and he brings a פסוק to prove it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: Circumcision is great, because even with all the מצוות that אברהם אבינו did, he was not called complete until he was circumcised. As it says: 'Walk before Me and be complete.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives his reason why מילה is great and supports it with a פסוק about אברהם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם had already done many מצוות. Still, הקב"ה told him to 'be complete' only when He gave him the מצוה of מילה. That shows מילה is what made him complete.

keyTerms.meaning: When said with no name, it means רבי יהודה הנשיא

phrases.english: Rabbi says: Great is circumcision,
phrases.notes: 'רבי' with no name is רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: for despite all the מצוות that Abraham our father did,
he was not called complete until he was circumcised,
as it says: 'Walk before Me and be complete.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 17:1. These words open the passage where אברהם is commanded about מילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another reason added to the list. This one is backed by a פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מילה is great because it made אברהם 'complete' in a way all his other מצוות did not.

steps.title: Another view: the world was created only because of circumcision
steps.stepSummary: A final view says that without מילה, הקב"ה would not have created the world. It proves this from a פסוק in ירמיהו about 'My covenant day and night'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: Circumcision is great, because if not for it, הקב"ה would not have created His world. As it says: 'Thus says ה׳: If not for My covenant day and night, I would not have set up the laws of heaven and earth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The list ends with the biggest praise of all: the whole world exists because of מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says heaven and earth depend on a 'covenant day and night'. This view reads that covenant as מילה, since it stays on a person's body at every moment, day and night. So the world's existence is tied to מילה.

keyTerms.meaning: My covenant (here read as the ברית מילה)
The laws or order of heaven and earth

steps.whatToRemember: Each תנא opens with 'גדולה מילה' and adds a reason: thirteen covenants were made over it (רבי ישמעאל), it overrides שבת (רבי יוסי), משה was punished at once for delaying it (רבי יהושע בן קרחה), it overrides נגעים (רבי נחמיה), it made אברהם complete (רבי), and the world was created for it (דבר אחר).

phrases.english: Another explanation: Great is circumcision,
for if not for it, would not have created
the Holy One, Blessed be He, His world,
as it says: 'Thus says ה׳:
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 33:25

phrases.english: If not for My covenant, day and night,
phrases.notes: The covenant that is with a person 'day and night' is read as מילה, because it is always on the body.

phrases.english: I would not have set up the laws of heaven and earth.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the list with the broadest praise, again backed by a פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מילה is great because the world was created for its sake.

steps.title: משה's merits did not protect him when he was lax about מילה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהושע בן קרחה: מילה is so great that all of משה's merits did not protect him when he was lax about it, as the פסוק says הקב"ה sought to kill him.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A ברייתא teaches: רבי יהושע בן קרחה says, מילה is great, because all the merits משה רבינו had did not protect him when he was lax about מילה, as it says: "And ה׳ met him and sought to kill him."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by bringing a ברייתא that gives the full version of רבי יהושע בן קרחה's statement from the משנה, including its proof from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said only that משה was not given even an hour's delay. Here the ברייתא adds that משה was lax about the מילה, and that his great merits did not save him. This shows how serious the מצוה of מילה is.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught in a ברייתא (a teaching from the time of the משנה)
Merits, credits earned from doing מצוות
Did not stand up for him; did not protect him

phrases.english: GEMARA: It is taught in a ברייתא:
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha says:
Great is circumcision,
for all the merits that Moshe our teacher performed
did not protect him
when he was lax about the circumcision,
as it is said:
"And ה׳ met him and sought to kill him."
phrases.notes: שמות 4:24

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by expanding רבי יהושע בן קרחה's statement from the משנה (step 12).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מילה is so great that משה's many merits did not protect him when he was lax about it.

steps.title: רבי says משה was not lax, but was caught in a real bind
steps.stepSummary: רבי rejects the claim that משה was lax. Doing the מילה and then traveling would endanger the baby, and waiting three days would go against הקב"ה's command to go to מצרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: Heaven forbid that משה רבינו was lax about מילה! Rather, this is what he said: If I do the מילה and leave, it is dangerous, as it says, "And it was on the third day, when they were in pain." If I do the מילה and wait three days, הקב"ה told me, "Go, return to מצרים."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי pushes back against the ברייתא. He says משה was never lax, and he explains why משה had a good reason not to do the מילה right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי attacks the word "lax" (נתרשל) in רבי יהושע בן קרחה's statement. He shows that משה had two bad options. Traveling right after the מילה would put the baby in danger, since the pain lasts until the third day. Waiting three days would mean delaying הקב"ה's order to go now. So holding off was not negligence.

keyTerms.meaning: Heaven forbid; strong rejection of an idea
If I circumcise and go out on the journey
And I will wait or delay

steps.confusionAlert: רבי is not saying that מילה is less important. He agrees משה was punished. He only rejects the idea that משה was lazy or careless about the מצוה.

phrases.english: Rabbi said:
phrases.notes: "רבי" on its own means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: Heaven forbid that Moshe our teacher
was lax about the circumcision!
Rather, this is what he said:
If I circumcise and set out,
it is a danger,
as it is said:
"And it was on the third day, when they were in pain, etc."
phrases.notes: בראשית 34:25. This is about the people of שכם after their מילה.

phrases.english: If I circumcise and wait three days,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, told me:
"Go, return to Egypt."
phrases.notes: שמות 4:19. משה understood this to mean he had to go right away.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי: חַס וְשָׁלוֹם שֶׁמּשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ נִתְרַשֵּׁל מִן הַמִּילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the claim in step 16 that משה was negligent about the מילה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the description of משה as lax, not the fact that he was punished.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא ignores that משה faced a real conflict: danger to the baby on one side, and הקב"ה's command to leave right away on the other.

steps.title: Then why was משה punished?
steps.stepSummary: Once רבי shows that משה was not lax, the גמרא asks why משה was punished at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then for what reason was משה punished?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. רבי's defense of משה leaves the punishment in the פסוק unexplained, so the גמרא asks what the punishment was for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק clearly says הקב"ה sought to kill משה, so there must have been some fault. Since it was not the delay of the מילה itself, the גמרא now needs a different reason. That answer comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: But for what reason
was Moshe punished?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from רבי's defense in step 17, which removed the ברייתא's explanation of the punishment.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What wrong did משה do that caused the punishment described in שמות 4:24, if he was not lax about the מילה?
